lead: Valencia’s Great Festival since the 14th century. Historic procession, medieval dances, the eleven Rocas pulled by horses and the struggle between Virtue and the Seven Deadly Sins in the streets of the historic centre.

The Corpus of Valencia is not just a religious procession: it is a total cultural spectacle that combines medieval theatre, ancestral dances, historic floats and a good dose of popular humour. Beyond the Catholic meaning of the festival, the Corpus is a living showcase of the coexistence of the festive, symbolic, metaphorical and religious spirit of Valencian society.

All its events take place in the historic centre of Valencia — Cathedral, Plaza de la Virgen, Plaza de Manises, Calle Cavallers and Calle Avellanes — and are open and free to attend. The Asociación Amics del Corpus de la Ciudad de València has been fundamental in the recovery and upkeep of this centuries-old tradition.

items.title: Transfer of the Rocas
items.subtitle: 11 triumphal carts · Alameditas de Serranos → Plaza de la Virgen
items.body: On Friday night, the eleven triumphal carts known as Rocas are solemnly moved from their usual home in the Casa de las Rocas to the Plaza de la Virgen, where they remain on display until Sunday’s procession. The Rocas are wooden structures shaped like an old ship that carry sculptural groups with episodes from the Old and New Testaments. Their origin is dated between 1373 and 1392, and the oldest of those that survive today — “La Diablera” — date from the 16th century. Pulled by horses specially harnessed for the occasion, their night-time parade officially opens the big days of the Corpus. The most recent is “El Santo Cáliz”, which paraded for the first time in 2001 and was blessed by Pope John Paul II.
facts: Friday · 20:00 · From Alameditas de Serranos to Plaza de la Virgen · Free access

items.title: La Nit d’Albaes
items.subtitle: Traditional songs · Route from the Casa de las Rocas
items.body: After the transfer of the Rocas, Friday night fills with traditional Valencian music at the Nit d’Albaes. The singers follow the usual route starting from the Casa de las Rocas, performing the albaes — Valencian folk songs of a festive nature, sung in the small hours. It is one of the most intimate and authentic events of the Corpus, letting you live the festival with the most genuine sounds of Valencian musical tradition.
facts: Friday · 23:30 · From the Casa de las Rocas · Route through the historic centre

items.title: La Poalà · La Penja de Poals
items.subtitle: The funniest moment of the Corpus · Buckets of water from the balconies
items.body: On Saturday at midday, the streets of Cavallers and Avellanes become the stage for one of the most popular and fun moments of the Corpus: the Poalà. Neighbours hang pozales (buckets) from the balconies and, when the “soldiers of King Herod” of the Cabalgata del Convite pass by, greet them with buckets of water. The joke has its reply and those below strike back. It is an old tradition of festive character and good humour that combines popular satire with religious celebration, and each year fills those streets of El Carmen district with laughter, water and neighbourhood spirit.
facts: Saturday · 12:00 · Streets Cavallers and Avellanes · Bring clothes you do not mind getting wet

items.title: Els Misteris · Representation of the Mysteries
items.subtitle: 15th-century medieval theatre · Staged by children · Biblical passages
items.body: On Saturday afternoon, the Plaza de la Virgen hosts the Representació dels Misteris: three short theatre pieces dating from the 15th century, staged by children, which tell biblical passages related to the characters who will parade the next day in the Cabalgata del Convite and the Procession. It is one of the oldest theatrical traditions in Valencia, a survivor of the medieval religious theatre that filled the city’s streets in the 15th century. They combine a didactic character with the visual spectacle of historic costumes and the setting of the Plaza de la Virgen lit up at dusk.
facts: Saturday · 18:00 · Plaza de la Virgen · Free access · Performed by children

items.title: Cabalgata del Convite · La Moma i els Momos
items.subtitle: The Capellà de les Roques · La Moma · 7 deadly sins · Traditional dances
items.body: The Cabalgata del Convite is the great popular spectacle of the Corpus. From the Plaza de Manises, the Capellà de les Roques — mounted on a horse with a black caparison embroidered in silver — leads the procession inviting the people to the Corpus Procession, just as the jurors of Valencia did from 1516. Behind him parade the most emblematic dances: La Moma i els Momos — the oldest and most specific dance of the Valencian Corpus, in which Virtue (La Moma, dressed in white and always played by a man) defeats the Seven Deadly Sins (Els Momos, in black and yellow costume and masks) — together with Els Arquets, Els Pastorets, Els Llauradors and Els Gegants i Nanos. All enlivened with dolçaina and tabalet music.
facts: Sunday · 12:00 · Starts from Plaza de Manises · Goes along Cavallers, Plaza de la Virgen, Avellanes · Free access

items.title: Pas de les Roques · Passage of the Rocas
items.subtitle: 11 triumphal carts pulled by horses · Route through the historic centre
items.body: On Sunday afternoon, the eleven Rocas again travel the streets of the historic centre, this time ahead of the Solemn Procession. Pulled by harnessed horses, they parade along the streets of Cavallers, Plaza del Tossal, Mercat, María Cristina, San Vicent, Plaza de la Reina, del Mar, Avellanes and up to the Palau Arzobispal. It is the moment when the public can admire these monumental medieval floats — some several metres high — up close, moving through the narrow streets of the historic centre, an image with no equal in any other Spanish festival.
facts: Sunday · 16:30 · Starts from Calle Cavallers · Goes through the historic centre · Free access

items.title: The Solemn Procession
items.subtitle: The central event · The Custodia · La Senyera · Biblical characters · Municipal Band
items.body: The Solemn Procession is the central and most majestic event of the Corpus. It leaves from the Puerta de los Apóstoles of the Cathedral at 19:00 on Sunday and tours the Ciutat Vella district. It is opened by La Senyera of the city flanked by Les Banderoles, carried by the three Kings of Arms in white wigs and beards. Behind them parade characters from the Old and New Testaments, the Carpenters’ Guild, dances, the Gegants i Nanos, the eleven Misteris with their biblical figures (King Herod, Saint Christopher, the Tarasca, the Dragon of Sant Jordi...). The climax is the Custodia — the essential element of the Corpus — preceded by the Archbishop of Valencia. The whole procession is enlivened by the Municipal Symphonic Band.
facts: Sunday · 19:00 · Puerta de los Apóstoles of the Cathedral
Sunday · 19:00 · Leaves from the Puerta de los Apóstoles of the Cathedral · Free access

blocks.title: Tips for experiencing the Corpus of Valencia
items: For Saturday’s Poalà on Cavallers and Avellanes, wear clothes you can get wet — the buckets of water are plentiful and accurate
Sunday’s Cabalgata del Convite is the most colourful event — arrive at 11:30 at the Plaza de Manises to get a good spot
To see the Rocas up close, Friday night’s transfer is the best moment — by day you see the procession, but from a distance
Sunday’s Solemn Procession at 19:00 is very long — choose a fixed spot on Calle Cavallers or in the Plaza de la Virgen
The Casa de las Rocas (Carrer de les Roques, 2) can be visited all year round to see the medieval floats up close
The Corpus is celebrated in the medieval historic centre — it is the perfect walk for getting to know the Valencia of the 14th century at the same time
